title: BMO demonstrates quantum computing milestone for AI and machine learning
excerpt: BMO has demonstrated what it describes as a quantum utility milestone in a machine learning application, to explore how quantum computing could improve AI models used in financial services.
content:
BMO has demonstrated what it describes as a quantum utility milestone in a machine learning application, to explore how quantum computing could improve AI models used in financial services.

The bank said the project showed how quantum computing can help identify the most relevant information within complex datasets, allowing AI models to generate insights using less data than conventional approaches.

BMO believes the technology could eventually support applications including client modelling, fraud and risk detection, and more personalised banking services.

The project was developed with the Democritus University of Thrace using IBM quantum systems, including the IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processor. IBM's quantum research team also reviewed the work.

According to BMO, the application achieved quantum utility, meaning it performed calculations at a scale that exact classical computing methods cannot practically reproduce.

The research focuses on a machine learning process known as feature selection, which identifies the most relevant variables within large datasets before a model begins analysis.

BMO and its research partners adapted the Proxy Quantum Games framework to treat each data feature as a "player" in a quantum game, allowing the quantum computer to rank the importance of different variables.

The bank said the approach produced results comparable to traditional feature selection techniques while requiring between one and two orders of magnitude fewer data samples.

BMO joined the IBM Quantum Network in February 2025 as part of a wider strategy to investigate practical applications for quantum computing. The bank has also established the BMO Institute for Applied Artificial Intelligence & Quantum to oversee AI governance and quantum research across the organisation.

Kristin Milchanowski, chief AI and quantum officer at BMO, said that demonstrating quantum utility is an important milestone for BMO and an exciting step forward for the broader financial services industry.

“While we remain in the early stages of application development, these projects show how quantum computing can help solve business problems in new ways,” she added.”This work builds on years of research, collaboration and innovation focused on identifying practical applications that create value for clients, employees and shareholders.”
